facts.statement: Fossils of Stagonosuchus were found in the Middle Triassic Manda Formation in Tanzania.
facts.quote: Fossils have been recovered from the Middle Triassic Manda Formation in Tanzania that are Anisian in age.

facts.statement: Stagonosuchus lived during the Anisian age of the Middle Triassic period.
facts.quote: Fossils have been recovered from the Middle Triassic Manda Formation in Tanzania that are Anisian in age.

facts.statement: Stagonosuchus is classified as an extinct paracrocodylomorph that may be a loricatan synonymous with Prestosuchus or a poposauroid.
facts.quote: Stagonosuchus is an extinct genus of paracrocodylomorph, possibly a loricatan synonymous with Prestosuchus or a poposauroid.

facts.statement: Unlike other rauisuchians, Stagonosuchus has only a slight thickening on the ilium instead of a prominent ridge.
facts.quote: Unlike other rauisuchians, which have a prominent ridge on the ilium called the supra-acetabular buttress that overlies the femur, Stagonosuchus possesses only a slight thickening on the surface of the bone.

facts.statement: The pubis bone in Stagonosuchus is broad and plate-like, differing from the narrower pubis with a foot-like extension seen in other genera.
facts.quote: In Stagonosuchus, the pubis is broad and plate like, while in other genera it is narrower and may have a prominent "foot" like that of some theropod dinosaurs.

facts.statement: The vertebrae of Stagonosuchus have constricted centra, though less so than in other rauisuchians like Saurosuchus.
facts.quote: The centra of the vertebrae are constricted to some extent, though not as much as in other rauisuchians such as Saurosuchus.

facts.statement: Neural canals in Stagonosuchus extend into the vertebrae, creating deep concavities.
facts.quote: In the vertebrae, the neural canals (through which the spinal cord would pass) extend into the centra, forming deep concavities.

facts.statement: Stagonosuchus vertebrae feature many laminae, which are ridges of bone.
facts.quote: Stagonosuchus also has many laminae, or ridges of bone on the vertebrae.

facts.statement: Friedrich von Huene first classified Stagonosuchus as a rauisuchid when he named the genus in 1938.
facts.quote: Friedrich von Huene, who named the genus in 1938, first classified Stagonosuchus as a rauisuchid.

facts.statement: A 2010 study placed Stagonosuchus in a basal position within Rauisuchia, outside both Rauisuchidae and Prestosuchidae.
facts.quote: A 2010 study on archosaurian phylogeny found Stagonosuchus to be outside both Rauisuchidae and Prestosuchidae in a more basal position within Rauisuchia.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Stagonosuchus is a second species of Prestosuchus or a distinct genus outside Loricata.
facts.quote: However, a study from the same year did not recover both as sister taxa, and the 2024 phylogenetic analysis recovered Stagonosuchus outside Loricata and suggested that it could be included within Poposauroidea instead.

facts.statement: A 2011 study identified Ticinosuchus as the closest relative of Stagonosuchus, despite significant size differences.
facts.quote: A 2011 study found Ticinosuchus to be the closest relative of Stagonosuchus despite a conspicuous difference in size between the two forms (Ticinosuchus is much more gracile than the larger Stagonosuchus).

facts.statement: Stagonosuchus belongs to the parent group Suchia.
Stagonosuchus is classified as a reptile.
The type species of the genus Stagonosuchus is Stagonosuchus nyassicus.
